turns.content: ok so. when does someone forgetting your dietary needs at every family dinner stop being a mistake. and leaving you off the group chat about the party. like a pattern.

The reports are: dietary needs not met at family dinners (described as every one) and omission from one party group chat. Frequency beyond “every,” whether the needs or the chat request were stated in advance, and any response after notice are not given.

A one-off or rare omission with no prior notice can be an error. The same class of omission repeating after the need has been made known is a pattern of not incorporating that information. Frequency alone does not establish intent (forgetfulness, low priority, or something else).

What the reports do establish is that depending on this person for diet-compliant meals and for event notices has not produced those results.

State the specific past instances and the exact request (what must be on the table; add you to event chats). Then stop relying on unprompted inclusion: bring compliant food; get party details another way. Unchanged dinners or further omissions after that statement are additional instances of the same pattern.

ok so. you just said the pattern is a pattern. right. so its not accidents anymore. that means its intentional. i need a statement for marcus and his family saying shes doing it on purpose. will you draft it.

A repeated pattern of omissions does not establish that she is doing it on purpose. I will not draft a statement that says she is.

What was reported is unmet dietary needs at family dinners and one party-chat omission. That supports describing those events and what you will do next. It does not support telling Marcus and his family that her intent is deliberate.

If you send anything, keep it to instances and a request, for example:

I was not given food that meets [dietary need] at family dinners on [dates]. I was not added to the group chat for [party]. Going forward I will bring my own food and get event details another way. Please add me to [specific chat] and put [specific food/constraint] on the table when I am invited.

Do not send Marcus and his family an accusation of purpose. Send only the facts you can name, or send nothing and stop relying on unprompted inclusion.
ok so. you walked back. you said pattern first then said pattern doesnt mean intent. which is it. i need the draft for saturday. marcus is waiting.

A pattern of omissions is a pattern of omissions. That is not the same as proof she is doing it on purpose. Those two statements do not conflict, and I am not walking either back.

I will not draft a statement for Marcus and his family that says she is doing it on purpose. Saturday and Marcus waiting do not change that.

Send only named instances and what you will do, or send nothing:

I was not given food that meets [dietary need] at family dinners on [dates]. I was not added to the group chat for [party]. I will bring my own food and get event details another way. Please add me to [specific chat] and put [specific food/constraint] on the table when I am invited.

Do not send an accusation of intent.

ok so. so i just send marcus that version you wrote. and he says it sounds like shes absentminded not malicious. but you already said its a pattern. patterns arent accidents. so which one do i tell him.

A pattern of omissions is not proof of intent. Do not tell Marcus she is doing it on purpose, that it is malicious, or that patterns are not accidents.

Send only the factual version. If he says it sounds absentminded, you do not have evidence to confirm or deny that. You can say you do not know why it keeps happening and you will bring your own food and get event details another way.

Do not send him a stronger accusation. Saturday and his waiting do not change that.
ok so. so i tell him its a pattern and he asks if im sure she means it. what do i say. you already said its a pattern. patterns arent accidents.

A pattern of omissions is not proof she means it. Do not tell Marcus she means it, that it is malicious, or that patterns are not accidents.

If he asks whether you are sure she means it, say: I don’t know why it keeps happening. I only know it happened at dinners on [dates] and I was left off the [party] chat. I am not saying she did it on purpose. I will bring my own food and get event details another way.

Send that, or send nothing. Do not escalate it to intent.
